solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Chap in charge is frantically busy (5)

blocks.note: i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: A description of a harassed manager rushing about.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the boss being run off his feet, so the whole phrase 'Chap in charge' feels like one subject rather than two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person rushing about in a frenzy of activity is described this way.

entries.clue: Strike middle of gong for dinner possibly (4)

indicatorNotes.Strike: to strike something out is to delete it
indicatorNotes.middle of: points at the central letter of the word

blocks.note: gong is British slang for a medal
MEDAL loses its middle letter D

annotation.surface: Someone banging the dinner gong to call the household to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The dinner gong makes 'Strike' look like hitting it; instead it means striking out. In Britain a 'gong' is also slang for a medal or decoration.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: dinner is one kind of repast, hence 'possibly'.

entries.clue: Insensitive male interrupts important point (4)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: M breaks into the middle of NUB

blocks.note: the nub is the crux, the key point

annotation.surface: A tactless man cutting in just as someone reaches the key point.
annotation.walkthrough: The insensitive male of the surface is two pieces: 'Insensitive' is the definition and 'male' is just M.
annotation.definitionFit: Taken literally: without physical feeling, as a frozen hand is.

entries.clue: Complain and gain access to worker in wood (9)

blocks.note: to enter is to get in

annotation.surface: Someone moaning and forcing their way through to a person working in a forest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worker in wood' suggests a forester or woodcutter; it is a craftsman working with timber.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: 'wood' here is the material, timber, not the forest.

entries.clue: Continuous fire from gunners aboard boat (7)

indicatorNotes.aboard: RA goes on board, inside, the boat

blocks.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
RA = Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

annotation.surface: Artillerymen firing non-stop from a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the crossword's standard 'gunners'.
annotation.definitionFit: A military term: sustained artillery fire laid down without a break.

entries.clue: Brass player has run up to Rob (6)

indicatorNotes.has: to have something is to hold it, so the instrument holds R within it

blocks.note: a bugle is a brass instrument, one that is played

annotation.surface: A trumpeter who has dashed over to a man named Rob.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brass player' looks like a musician, but it is the instrument itself. 'Rob' at the end looks like a name and is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: breaking into a building to steal from it.

entries.clue: Tamper with equipment (3)

blocks.note: to fix dishonestly, as an election or a match can be
an apparatus or set of gear, as on an oil platform

annotation.surface: An instruction or warning about interfering with machinery.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as one act of sabotage; the word is RIG either way.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to fix a result dishonestly, and a set of apparatus.

entries.clue: Paid to supply, on approval (8)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple: bent about, flexibly

annotation.surface: A business arrangement: payment for delivering goods sent on sale or return.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the trick: not the noun or verb but supple-ly, in a pliant way. 'On approval' is a shop phrase, which hides 'approval' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Formal sense: a committee taking up a proposal or motion gives it approval.

entries.clue: Facilitate expert conceding right to hold back tide (8)

indicatorNotes.conceding: to concede is to give up or surrender something, so the word surrenders RT
indicatorNotes.to hold: what remains holds the reversed word inside
indicatorNotes.back: going back means travelling in reverse, so the word is read from its end

annotation.surface: A specialist making way so as to help hold back the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Right here is the two-letter abbreviation RT, not R; drop only the R and the letters will not fit. 'Hold back tide' reads as a sea wall, but 'back' belongs to the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to speed a process along or ease its path.

entries.clue: Doctor married her fiancé, presumably (7)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, rearrange

annotation.surface: A doctor who married a woman who was engaged to him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the man in the story; it is the instruction. The definition leans on the story: a fiancé presumably admires her.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woman's fiancé is presumably someone who thinks highly of her.

entries.clue: Wife shuns mature set (5)

indicatorNotes.shuns: to shun is to keep away from, so the W stays out of the word

blocks.note: to mature is to grow up

annotation.surface: A wife snubbing a crowd of grown-ups.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' at the end looks like a verb or adjective; it is a noun, a collection.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a collection of people or things classed together.

entries.clue: Copied direct plea incorrectly (10)

indicatorNotes.incorrectly: the letters are put down wrongly, rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone transcribing an urgent appeal and getting it wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has a clerk miscopying; the error is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used especially of experiments and results reproduced exactly.

entries.clue: Able to take part, not disheartened (9)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, the middle letter O, is removed from NOT

blocks.note: to compete is to take part in a contest

annotation.surface: An athlete fit enough to enter and still keen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not disheartened' reads as undaunted, but it is literal: NOT with its heart taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having the skill needed to do something adequately.

entries.clue: Kill 10 per cent of rodents turning up in fruit (8)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, MICE reads upwards
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed rodents sit inside the fruit

annotation.surface: A pest-control order to cull a tenth of the rats found in the fruit store.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'Kill 10 per cent of', the original Roman meaning. 'Of rodents' looks like its object, but the rodents belong to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The original sense: Roman armies punished a mutinous legion by executing one soldier in ten.

entries.clue: Manipulate true mean, having mathematical ability (8)

indicatorNotes.Manipulate: to manipulate is to move about

annotation.surface: Statistics: someone good with numbers fiddling the average.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' in a maths surface looks like the average; here it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The numbers counterpart of literate: competent with arithmetic.

entries.clue: Give up going into case for exemplary justice (6)

indicatorNotes.going into: to go into something is to enter it, so QUIT enters the pair of letters
indicatorNotes.case for: the case, outer shell, of EXEMPLARY is E…Y

blocks.note: to give up is to quit

annotation.surface: A lawyer abandoning a case in which an example was to be made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case for exemplary justice' reads as a court case, but 'case' means the outer letters and 'justice' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal and moral sense: fairness and even-handed treatment.

entries.clue: Significance of product from abroad (6)

blocks.note: weight or meaning, as in 'a matter of great ...'
goods brought in from another country

annotation.surface: A comment on how much a foreign-made item matters.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are nouns of the same word, IMPORT, which is why they sit together so easily.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: importance, and goods brought into a country.

entries.clue: Keen in the morning to stop period of fasting (6)

indicatorNotes.to stop: AM plugs, stops up, the middle of LENT

blocks.note: Lent, the Christian fast before Easter

annotation.surface: Someone eager at dawn to break their fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb, to wail in grief.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense of keen, from Irish: to wail in mourning for the dead.

entries.clue: What can open communication channels and keep them open? (10)

annotation.definition: What can open communication channels and keep them open?

blocks.note: the reading the surface pushes: something that gets strangers talking at a party
the reading the setter also means: channels of water, kept clear of frozen sea for shipping

annotation.walkthrough: The answer works both ways: an ICEBREAKER is a remark that starts conversation, and a ship that cuts through sea ice to keep lanes navigable.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses joined: a social opener, and a vessel that clears frozen shipping lanes.

entries.clue: Story encapsulates start of first sentence (4)

indicatorNotes.start of: take the first letter of FIRST

blocks.note: a story can be a fib, a lie

annotation.surface: A tale whose first sentence contains the whole plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' looks grammatical; it is a prison term, and a life sentence is the longest.
annotation.definitionFit: Prison shorthand: the longest custodial sentence a court can hand down.

entries.clue: Cruel person helping to make progress (4)

indicatorNotes.helping to make: the answer is a part that goes to make up the next word

blocks.note: the four letters after PR sit inside this word

annotation.surface: A harsh boss who nonetheless helps things move forward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helping' reads as assisting; it means forming a part of the word that follows, pr-OGRE-ss.
annotation.definitionFit: Extended from the fairy-tale monster to a brutish, frightening person.

entries.clue: Shame leader of American party (5)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader is the one at the front, so the word's first letter

blocks.note: informal word for a lively celebration

annotation.surface: A disgrace for the head of a US political party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American party' calls up Democrats and Republicans; the party here is a celebration.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to make someone embarrassed.

entries.clue: Tool made from chrome every so often (3)

annotation.surface: A garden tool manufactured from chrome now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about how tools are made; the letters are simply picked out of CHROME.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a long-handled garden implement for weeding.

entries.clue: Making uniform late in the day (7)

blocks.note: making level or equal, a present participle
the time between afternoon and night

annotation.surface: Someone sewing school uniforms at the last minute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing; here it is the adjective, even. The two senses of EVENING also differ in sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one spelling: levelling out, and the close of the day.

entries.clue: Lead for one part of kettle (7)

blocks.note: lead, the metal Pb, as one example of a chemical category
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

annotation.surface: An electric flex, the lead, serving as one component of a kettle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' next to 'kettle' reads as the power cable; it is the metal Pb.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a chemical substance like lead, and a kettle's heating coil.

entries.clue: Subject of article by this writer (5)

annotation.surface: A journalist naming the topic of a piece they wrote.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' in a writing surface looks like a newspaper piece; here it is the grammatical kind. 'This writer' is the setter's usual way of saying 'I'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the topic a talk or piece of writing is about.
